newsitem.title: UK: UK's power market has manual back-up - watchdog.
newsitem.headline: UK's power market has manual back-up - watchdog.

text.p: Britain's electricity supply market could use a manual back-up system if planned computer systems for liberalisation by September 1998 go badly awry, Stephen Littlechild, head of industry watchdog Offer, said on Wednesday.
He told parliament's trade and industry select committee that a manual system was part of contingency plans but reassured that there was currently "no reason to change" timetables.

Current plans call for electricity companies to set up computer systems to handle both internal changes and complicated interfaces between companies, the supply market and producers, which liberalisation of the supply market will require.
"Competition will be able to take place and there will not be any chaos," Littlechild said.
He said companies had given assurances that their information technology (IT) systems would be able to cope with liberalisation, which will be phased in from April 1998.
Offer had taken steps to monitor what companies were doing, Littlechild added.

He said that Offer would be "firming up proposals" for phasing in liberalisation "as soon as we can," but added that he had only just received all responses to a consultation paper issued in December.
Out of 40 or so comments received, only one thought the market should not be phased but freed up in one step, Offer's Tony Boorman said.
Boorman added that Offer hoped to make a further statement on progress in March.
"It seems that arrangements (by companies) are mostly satisfactory and they are aware of the sensibility of phasing (liberalisation) in," Littlechild said.
He said Offer would like to have licence conditions necessary for liberalisation finalised by October so that any appeal to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) could be judged by April 1998.
